title: What are Components?
overview: Components are the building blocks of every React Native application. Every screen you see in a mobile app is made up of multiple components. React Native provides built-in components like View, Text, Image, Button, TextInput, ScrollView, and FlatList, and you can also create your own custom components.

example.title: Using Components

title: Functional Components
overview: A functional component is simply a JavaScript function that returns JSX. It is the recommended way to create components in modern React Native because it is simple, lightweight, and supports React Hooks.

example.title: Functional Component Example

title: Class Components
overview: Class components were commonly used before React Hooks were introduced. They use JavaScript classes and lifecycle methods to manage state and behavior. Today, they are mostly found in older React Native projects.

example.title: Class Component Example

title: Built-in Components
overview: React Native includes many built-in components that help you build mobile interfaces. These components are optimized for Android and iOS and behave like native UI elements.

example.title: Common Built-in Components
example.content:
View
Text
Image
Button
TextInput
ScrollView
FlatList
Pressable
TouchableOpacity
SafeAreaView

title: Creating Custom Components
overview: Custom components are reusable components created by developers. They help reduce duplicate code and make applications easier to maintain.

example.title: Custom Component Example

title: Reusing Components
overview: One of the biggest advantages of components is reusability. Instead of writing the same UI multiple times, you can create a component once and use it anywhere in your application.

example.title: Using a Custom Component

title: Component Naming Rules
overview: Component names must always start with a capital letter. React uses this convention to distinguish custom components from built-in HTML or React Native elements.

title: Best Practices for Components
overview: Keep components small, reusable, and focused on a single responsibility. Organize related components into folders and avoid writing very large components that handle multiple tasks.

example.title: Best Practices
example.content:
• Keep components small.
• Reuse components whenever possible.
• Use meaningful names.
• Place each component in its own file.
• Avoid duplicate UI code.

title: Topic Summary
overview: You learned what components are, the difference between functional and class components, how to use built-in components, create custom components, reuse them, follow naming conventions, and write maintainable component-based applications.

example.title: Quick Revision
example.content:

✔ Functional components are recommended.

✔ Create reusable custom components.
